newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian group suggests Internet paedophile control.
newsitem.headline: Belgian group suggests Internet paedophile control.

text.p: A Belgian group fighting paedophile pornography on the Internet proposed on Wednesday a two-pronged approach combining legal enforcement and voluntary policing.
"There must be a lot of good will to achieve an effective control," the Movement Against Paedophilia on the Internet (MAPI) said in a statement.
MAPI, set up after the discovery in August of the bodies of four young girls who had died at the hands of a paedophile gang, brings together sociologists, academics and economists.
It proposed more stringent application of a 1995 Belgian law against child pornography, enabling the authorities to prosecute the issuer, consumer and Internet service provider.
MAPI said particular emphasis should be put on making the service providers aware of their responsibilities and trying to bring international authorities into the fray.

Complementing this would be a voluntary policing approach, persuading the service providers to dissuade their clients from posting child pornography on sites of the World Wide Web, and using a judicious dose of keyword patrolling.
"The Internet is not a diabolic invention, but it can be used aas a vehicle for messages that can harm the most vulnerable, like children," MAPI said.
